decisions.question: How the AWS-default allow-all egress is removed from both security groups (handoff section 4, point 1)
decisions.answer: In the template. The host security group declares its S3 prefix-list egress inline (which replaces its default rule) and its egress to the endpoint security group as a standalone AWS::EC2::SecurityGroupEgress. The endpoint security group declares its ingress from the host group inline and one inline egress entry, the documented loopback placeholder (IpProtocol -1, CidrIp 127.0.0.1/32), which replaces its default rule. The placeholder is accepted as the evidence of 'no egress': describe-security-group-rules will show that one egress rule on the endpoint group, with a Description that names it as the placeholder.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '1a'. The documented pattern (F-R4-1); no circular reference; no post-creation CLI edit of a template-managed resource, so no drift.
decisions.consequence: Register v2 DC-03 reads 'no other rules apart from the loopback placeholder that replaces AWS's default egress'. tests/test_aws_network_template.py pins the placeholder as the only CIDR rule in the template.

decisions.question: The VPC's default security group (handoff section 4, point 2)
decisions.answer: Lasting rule: the default security group of every project VPC carries no rule. CloudFormation cannot manage it, so after the stack is created the operator records its rules, revokes every ingress and egress rule by rule id (revoke-security-group-ingress/egress --security-group-rule-ids), and records the empty rule list; both records are R4 evidence. Nothing is ever attached to the default group. The rule holds for the lifetime of the VPC: a stack update never re-creates the default group, and the R12a collector checks that it is still empty.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '2b + record igen'. Cheap; DC-06 and DC-07 then hold for every security group in the VPC, not only the two the template manages.
decisions.consequence: R4 step sheet step 08 (before, revoke, after). R12a adds one check: the default security group of the VpcId in R4_outputs.json has zero rules. If the VPC is ever replaced, the step is repeated for the new VPC in that ticket.

decisions.question: S3 gateway endpoint policy (handoff section 4, point 3)
decisions.answer: One Allow statement, Principal '*', actions s3:GetObject, s3:ListBucket and s3:GetBucketLocation (read-only), resources arn:${AWS::Partition}:s3:::${ProjectName}-deploy-${AWS::AccountId} and its objects, with Condition StringEquals on both aws:ResourceAccount and aws:PrincipalAccount = ${AWS::AccountId}. The trail bucket is not named (CloudTrail writes service-side). The AL2023 repository buckets are not named (OD9: offline bundle). The SSM Agent's regional buckets are not named; R11 shows whether Run Command needs them. The runtime role is not named (it does not exist before R5); R5's role policy and R7's bucket policy narrow access further.
decisions.reason: Operator's answers '3a read-only' and '3c igen'. aws:PrincipalAccount refuses requests signed with another account's credentials, presigned URLs included, and anonymous requests; aws:ResourceAccount refuses every bucket outside the account; the bucket ARNs are the second belt. Nothing before R15/R16 writes to S3 from the host (F-R4-4).
decisions.consequence: If a later ticket needs an upload route from the host (R15 export, R16 DC-38 logs) or Run Command needs an SSM bucket (R11), that ticket adds a statement by an UPDATE change set, with evidence, and writes a successor to this record. R12b's F7 negative test (presigned PUT to an outside bucket refused) is unchanged.

decisions.question: Guard-test extension (handoff section 4, point 4)
decisions.answer: Both: (a) AWS::EC2::Route joins FORBIDDEN_RESOURCE_TYPES in tools/aws_template_guard.py, for every template, since no project template writes a route (the S3 gateway endpoint adds the one prefix-list route itself); a forbidden type is reported once, without a project-tag finding. (b) tests/test_aws_network_template.py pins the network template's shape: the eight resources, both DNS attributes, no public IP on launch, the host group's two egress rules and no ingress, the endpoint group's one ingress and the placeholder egress, the gateway endpoint on the one route table, the read-only policy whose every resource ends in ${AWS::AccountId} or ${AWS::AccountId}/*, both conditions, Name and project tags, and the contract outputs. UNTAGGABLE_TYPES is unchanged (F-R4-2).
